notes: Asserts that a permission dialog raised by a READ-ONLY tool produces its own waiting episode, exactly like one raised by a mutating tool — two DISTINCT episodes in ONE copilot session. WHY THIS IS EXPECTED TO PASS ON COPILOT: irrlicht's copilot parser is KIND-AGNOSTIC. parsePermissionRequested (core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go) reads only requestId — no kind, no tool name, no allowlist — and applyPermissionDeltas (core/pkg/tailer/tailer.go) folds ids into a SET, so two sequential permission.requested/permission.completed pairs drive TranscriptPermissionPending (tailer_metrics.go:656) true→false→true→false and the transcript_permission_prompt rule (state_classifier.go:152, TierTranscript) fires twice. The #1861 failure this row was written from (a nine-tool-name allowlist on the subscriber side) has nowhere to live on this adapter. AGENT SIDE: copilot CLI 1.0.78 treats a read as its own permission kind — its shipped schemas/session-events.schema.json carries PermissionRequestRead ('File or directory read permission request'), PermissionRequestUrl, and PermissionPromptRequestPathAccessKind = enum[read, shell, write]; the path dialog's own copy is 'This action may read the following path outside your allowed directory list' under the title 'Allow directory access'. All three prompt kinds (tool | path | url) route through PendingRequests.requestPermissionPrompt, which ends `mg(this.emit, r.event)` — the NON-ephemeral emitter — so the line is written to events.jsonl while the CLI sits blocked. The schema states the same thing in the type: PermissionRequestedEvent.ephemeral is a plain optional boolean, whereas ElicitationRequestedEvent.ephemeral is const:true, 'Always true for events that are transient and not persisted to the session event log on disk'. BIRTH SHAPE (unchanged from 2-11 / 2-19, taken from live recordings): the transient proc-<PID> presession is born ready, but the REAL session — the ~/.copilot/session-state/<dir> name, a DIFFERENT id — is born DIRECTLY into working, because copilot creates the directory at launch with only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl at the first prompt, so the open turn is already on disk at discovery. session_birth and the first turn_start are ONE phase. THE INTERMEDIATE READY IS EXPECTED, AND IS WHY gate1_release / gate2_waiting ARE SEPARATE PHASES: copilot closes a turn after EVERY tool call, so after gate 1 is approved the real arc is waiting → working → (tool) → ready → working → waiting rather than the row's literal waiting → working → waiting. The row's criteria are about the two episodes being distinct and each being its own, which this shape satisfies more strongly than a merged one; no phase here forbids a ready between the gates. A recording that shows ONE merged waiting episode does NOT satisfy this row — re-drive as two turns. THE TAIL IS A kind-ANCHORED WINDOW, NOT A ready HOLD: settle binds to the first ready after gate 2's release (which may be a mid-turn turn_end blip — copilot writes two assistant.turn_end per prompt when a tool is involved), so pinning duration_at_least_ms on it would fail for a reason unrelated to permissions. no_waiting_tail re-matches that same event as a kind:state_transition phase and carries the invariant over a 15s window instead — the 2-11 pattern, where checkDurationAtLeast is skipped for a phase with no expected_state and the duration defines only the invariant window. That window is the row's load-bearing trailing-idle claim: the session does not fall back to waiting after the last dialog closes. NOT VACUOUS ONLY IF BOTH GATES REALLY FIRED. A read target inside the allowed directory list is auto-approved and writes no permission.requested at all, which is indistinguishable in events.jsonl from the daemon missing the second gate. The cell's proof-of-gate is transcript-level and POSITIVE: two permission.requested lines with distinct requestIds, the second carrying a read-only descriptor (kind read|url, or path with accessKind read|shell) and no write signal. One line means INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass. See the cell's caveats for the environment properties that must be re-probed (COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1; the read target outside both the run cwd and the system temporary directory; no --add-dir; no COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS). OBSERVATIONS: the turn completes here (unlike 2-19, which terminates in waiting), so assistant.turn_end / session.usage_checkpoint land and cost + tokens are legitimately non-zero. model is deliberately UNPINNED — --model accepts only 'auto' on this account and the router picks per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5; record fills it from the recording.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the ExactName matcher binds the PID while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)

The real session (the session-state directory name — a DIFFERENT session_id) reconciles when events.jsonl appears at the first prompt, and is born DIRECTLY into working because the file already carries the open turn
copilot PID bound to the real session by cwd match

THE MUTATING HALF (the path 2-19 already covers): the shell write `echo written > out.txt` matches no approval rule, so copilot writes permission.requested {kind:shell, hasWriteFileRedirection:true} and blocks — TranscriptPermissionPending=true → transcript_permission_prompt → working → waiting, read from the transcript alone
The user answers the first dialog: permission.completed retires the requestId, openPermissions empties, and the session leaves waiting. The gated call then executes

THE ASSERTION THIS ROW ADDS: the READ-ONLY call (a file read outside copilot's default allowed directory list — cwd plus the system temp dir) raises its OWN dialog, and it produces its own waiting episode. It is not skipped, and it is not merged into the mutating tool's episode. Distinct requestId, second true→false→true cycle of TranscriptPermissionPending
The user answers the second dialog and the read executes — the read-only gate releases through exactly the same permission.completed edge as the mutating one
assistant.turn_end settles the session back to ready after the second approval. Final state is ready — the session does not remain waiting once the last dialog closes

THE TRAILING IDLE: re-matches the settle event and pins the invariant over the 15s that follow — no waiting episode reappears once both dialogs are closed. Carried as a kind-anchored window rather than a ready hold so copilot's mid-turn turn_end blip cannot fail it for a reason unrelated to permissions
